subject: Low-latency SLOs & multi-region routing - post-call follow-up
messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>

Subject: Post-call recap: low-latency SLOs & routing (notes + asks)

Hi Tara —

Thanks again for the call earlier. Quick recap and a few concrete asks so we can size the right config and routing policy for FinOps Co. Below is what I captured; please correct anything I got wrong and add numbers where you can.

Summary of goals we discussed
- Primary objective: provide sub-100ms tail latency for interactive streaming use cases in US, and predictable p99 behavior globally with failover.
- Regional requirements: US production first, EU for EU customers with data residency constraints, APAC for emerging player base (lower traffic initially).

What we need from you (short answers appreciated)
1) Peak and average request volume by region (RPS or requests/min): e.g. US peak = ? / sustained = ?
2) Concurrency: expected simultaneous open streaming sessions (typical and burst)
3) Typical request/response token lengths (avg input tokens / avg generated tokens)
4) Hard SLOs: p50/p95/p99 latency targets you must meet for streaming first-byte and token-by-token framing
5) Any absolute constraints on where PII or logs must live (EU-only processing, logging restrictions, retention windows)

What we recommend next (internal + external actions)
- Vivek will validate whether Hosted routing with dedicated regional pools is sufficient or if a Dedicated reservation per region is required to hit your p99 targets at scale.
- We'll produce a draft SLO matrix and a regional capacity sketch (attached initial notes).
- Proposed follow-up: technical sizing + procurement checklist meeting (30m) next week.

Quick notes from call (our interpretation)
- Streaming behavior: token-by-token flush desired, low inter-token latency (~<=50ms ideal) for UI responsiveness.
- Fallbacks: prefer region-local serving; if capacity constrained, route to nearest region with explicit consent and degraded SLOs.
- Security: SOC2 & data isolation items to be looped into procurement/security review.

Attachments: finops_slo_needs.xlsx (please fill), redwood_regional_routing_notes.pdf (initial sketch), proposal_slo_matrix_v1.pdf (draft)
HubSpot: HS-12345

Thanks — will follow up once we have the numbers you provided.

Jonas Weber

Jonas —

Thanks for the clear notes. Below are the numbers we can confirm quickly; I filled the attached spreadsheet with the same figures. Happy to refine in the follow-up.

Regional traffic (approx peak / sustained):
- US: peak 350 RPS, sustained 180 RPS (peak windows ~ 10–15 minutes during business hours)
- EU: peak 150 RPS, sustained 70 RPS
- APAC: peak 120 RPS, sustained 50 RPS (growth expected Q3)

Concurrency: typical 60 concurrent streaming sessions across all regions; burst to 120 for ~30s when a marketing push lands.

Token sizes: average input ~30 tokens, average generated ~120 tokens (we stream token-by-token to UI).

SLO targets (business-critical):
- Streaming first-byte p99: US <= 80ms, EU <= 120ms, APAC <= 180ms
- Inter-token latency (per-frame): target <= 50ms average, 95th <= 120ms

Data residency: EU customer data and any PII must remain within EU region at rest and during processing. Logs that contain PII must be stored in EU and retention not to exceed 90 days without express consent. Non-PII telemetry can be aggregated across regions.

Security/compliance: please include SOC 2 scope doc and an outline of audit logs (I cc'ed Vivek for the tech details). Procurement will want those docs in the next meeting.

Next steps: a technical sizing call + procurement/security review — are you available Tue/Wed next week? If not, propose Thu 10:00–10:30 ET.

Best,

Subject: Re: Post-call recap: low-latency SLOs & routing (notes + asks)

Hi Tara — thanks for the fast reply and the numbers. A few technical clarifications and preliminary recommendations from my side so procurement/architecture have visibility before the follow-up meeting.

Quick clarifications (please confirm):
- Is the EU requirement strict processing-in-EU (i.e., model weights + inference compute must be resident in EU), or is it acceptable to route/transform tokens in EU and forward anonymized payloads elsewhere? You indicated "must remain within EU" so I'm assuming compute+logs in-region.
- Any specific regional cloud/provider preferences (AWS eu-west-1, GCP europe-west2, etc.)?

Preliminary options to meet the SLOs you listed:
1) Dedicated regional pools (recommended for predictable p99): reserve capacity in US, EU, APAC. This minimizes cross-region network hops and gives us deterministic KV cache locality.
2) Hosted with latency-first routing + warm standby in each region: lower capex but risk of p99 spikes under high burst without dedicated reservation.

Streaming specifics and tuning notes:
- We can support token-by-token streaming via HTTP chunked responses or gRPC. For your inter-token <=50ms target, we recommend using gRPC streaming or HTTP/2 with Nagle disabled and client-side small flush intervals (server flush <20ms).
- KV cache: warmup your common prefixes or use a short-lived pre-warm during expected bursts (helps reduce cold-start token latency).
- Batching: at your stated avg token sizes, we expect batching to be constrained to maintain per-token latency — favor continuous small batches with concurrency tuning rather than larger micro-batches.

Preliminary capacity sketch (very rough):
- Given model family of ~7–13B (if using a medium open model) and 350 RPS peak US with streamed outputs at ~120 tokens, we'd estimate a need for X dedicated inference units (I'll provide exact GPU count after we select the model variant).
- If you choose a larger LLM (70B-class), you'll likely need dedicated GPUs in each region to hold KV cache and meet p99.

Routing behavior & failover:
- Primary: route by geo + latency-first policy.
- Fallback: nearest-region fallback with explicit lowered SLOs (we can tag requests that cross-region for reporting).

Attachments: regional_capacity_estimate.csv (very rough numbers). I'll produce a full SLO matrix and a recommended reservation config once we lock model choice.

I'll be available Tue/Wed for a deeper sizing call; Jonas will coordinate schedule.

-Vivek
